editorNote: Thanksgiving week keeps the Chronicle at the holiday electronics counter: GCE's Vectrex brings a self-contained vector display, Atari sells both a premium 5200 and the newly named 2600, and Apple II players keep Choplifter high on the year's software shelf.
morningLine: A built-in vector monitor, a crowded Atari cartridge wall, Apple II rescue missions, E.T. at the box office, and Lionel Richie on the radio define the week of November 22, 1982.

lead.headline: Vectrex Brings Vector Arcade Lines Home
lead.summary: General Consumer Electronics' Vectrex reached the 1982 holiday market as a self-contained game system with its own black-and-white vector monitor and color screen overlays, giving store demonstrators a sharp contrast to television-based consoles.
lead.confidence: Month-specific November 1982 launch; holiday-week emphasis inferred from release timing and retail context.

computerItems.headline: Atari 5200 Shares the Aisle With the Renamed 2600
computerItems.summary: Atari's November hardware story is split: the 5200 SuperSystem courts premium buyers while the former VCS carries the Atari 2600 name and the familiar cartridge library into the same shopping season.
computerItems.confidence: Month-specific November 1982 5200 release and VCS-to-2600 rename.

computerItems.label: Home Computer Desk
computerItems.headline: Commodore 64 Becomes the New Memory Pitch
computerItems.summary: The Commodore 64, introduced in 1982, gives dealers an easy showroom line: 64K of RAM, color graphics, sound, and a price aimed at families comparing computers and game machines.
computerItems.confidence: 1982 release and period positioning; not exact-day specific.

computerItems.label: Apple II Games
computerItems.headline: Choplifter Keeps the Apple II in the Game Conversation
computerItems.summary: Dan Gorlin's Choplifter, published by Broderbund for the Apple II in 1982, remains a showcase for computer-first action design while console shoppers fill the holiday aisles.
computerItems.confidence: 1982 Apple II release and Softalk reader-poll prominence.

market.headline: Holiday Counters Sell Screens, Memory, and Libraries
market.summary: Retailers can stage three different arguments at once: Vectrex has its own screen, Atari has a huge cartridge back catalog plus the 5200, and Commodore sells 64K as a family-computer number.
market.confidence: Synthesized from 1982 hardware launches and period retail positioning.

bbsNote.headline: Modem Note
bbsNote.summary: The mass market is still focused on consoles and low-cost computers, while 300-baud bulletin-board callers trade settings, game hints, and local phone numbers after hours.

curiosity.headline: Cinema Lobby
curiosity.summary: Box Office Mojo lists E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial as the weekly domestic box-office leader for November 26-December 2, 1982, keeping the film in front of the same families seeing E.T. cartridge ads.

briefs.headline: Lionel Richie Takes the Hot 100
briefs.summary: Billboard's Hot 100 for November 27, 1982 puts Lionel Richie's "Truly" at No. 1, followed by Laura Branigan's "Gloria" and Olivia Newton-John's "Heart Attack."

briefs.headline: E.T. Leads the Holiday Box Office
briefs.summary: For the domestic week of November 26-December 2, E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial is listed as the top film, with First Blood continuing its fall run.

briefs.headline: Apple II Poll Favors Action
